solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Initially supply tablets for upsets

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word supply

parts.note: tablets are pills

explanation.surface: Someone first hands out tablets to cure stomach upsets.
explanation.definitionFit: Spills are tumbles or falls, the noun sense of upsets.

clue.text: Manage to rescue

definitions.meaning: to manage something difficult is to succeed in pulling it off
to rescue someone is to get them away safely, for example from a sinking ship

explanation.walkthrough: The 'to' between the two definitions is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both succeed at a task and lift people off a wreck or cliff to safety.

clue.text: I rest at inn specially prepared for travellers

indicators.note: something specially prepared has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wanderers say they will rest at an inn got ready for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially prepared' signals an anagram of I REST AT INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerants are people who journey from place to place, so they are travellers.

clue.text: Islander getting fish, no English fellow (Scot?)

indicators.note: no means the letter for English is left out of the fish

parts.note: a sardine is a small fish
Ian is a man's name, Scottish in origin, hence the query

explanation.surface: An island native catches a fish, though he is not English but perhaps a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no English' takes E out of SARDINE, leaving SARDIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sardinian is a native of Sardinia, a Mediterranean island.

clue.text: A feature of rugby — heartless, despicable people!

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the scrum is a set piece in rugby

explanation.surface: A rant that rugby, robbed of its heart, attracts only contemptible types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle R out of SCRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous term for worthless, despicable people.

clue.text: Holy writings, Christian books buried in Irish hill

indicators.note: buried in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the seat of Ireland's high kings
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Sacred scriptures and Christian texts have been buried on an Irish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantras are Hindu and Buddhist sacred texts, holy writings of those traditions.

clue.text: Dish with duck — commotion when it's dry inside

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: inside means the dry piece goes within the commotion

parts.note: a melee is a confused scuffle, a commotion
TT, teetotal, means dry or not drinking

explanation.surface: A duck dish causes uproar when it turns out dry in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the dish's ingredient but is the cricket zero; 'when it's' is only link material.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a beaten egg dish, a dish made in a pan.

clue.text: Robbers making very good speed south

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means very good in crosswords
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Thieves make good time heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates are sea robbers who plunder ships.

clue.text: Second rescue vessel provided for island

parts.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A second lifeboat has been sent out to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small Channel Island, so it is an island.

clue.text: Express approval of an assertion audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the phrase is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: an assertion is a claim, so this is 'a claim'

explanation.surface: Someone voices praise for a statement out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to praise publicly, to express approval of someone.

clue.text: City left in danger after disturbance

indicators.note: after being disturbed the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city is left in peril after unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' looks like part of the city's peril in the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Leningrad was the Soviet name for the Russian city of St Petersburg.

clue.text: Came across aluminium — as an example of one?

parts.note: came across means met, encountered
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on aluminium and wonders whether it counts as a sample.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans back on aluminium: aluminium is an example of one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium is a classic instance of a metal element, which the definition invites.

clue.text: It spells an end for trout, being in acidic river

indicators.note: being in means the letter goes inside the sour word

parts.note: acidic means sour

indicators.note: an end for picks the last letter of the word trout

explanation.surface: Acid water in a river spells the end for the trout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It spells' is link material: the clue says this construction spells the answer. The Stour is a name shared by several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is a river in several English counties, such as Kent and Dorset.

clue.text: Direction given by senator misguidedly

indicators.note: misguidedly means the letters are wrongly directed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A senator misdirects someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor'-east is a contraction of north-east, a compass direction.

clue.text: Bad character hanging round end of street is a professional killer

indicators.note: hanging round means the scrambled letters sit around the other piece
bad means the letters are spoilt into a new arrangement
end of picks the final letter of the word street

explanation.surface: A villain loitering on a street corner is a hitman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges CHARACTER, and 'hanging round' puts that around T, the last letter of street.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-catcher kills rats for a living, a professional killer in a humorous sense.

clue.text: One's out to get this money

definitions.text: One's out to get this money

parts.words: One's out to get this money
parts.note: being out reads as being on strike, and the money is what the union pays a striking worker

explanation.definitionFit: Strike pay is the allowance a union gives members while they are on strike.

clue.text: The tenet I clarified after translation

indicators.note: translation turns the letters into something else, an anagram

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A principle someone explained once it had been translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after translation' signals an anagram of TENET I CLARIFIED; the definition is just 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, contrasted with the indefinite 'a'.

clue.text: Wrong direction when one's abandoned creed

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in a mistaken order
abandoned means the letter for one is dropped from direction

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A heretic took a wrong turn once he abandoned his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's abandoned' removes I from DIRECTION, and 'Wrong' rearranges the remaining DRECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a set of beliefs taught by a church, so a creed.

clue.text: Frontiersman given severe reprimand in court

indicators.note: in means the reprimand sits inside the court

parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: A pioneer gets a fierce dressing-down in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Davy Crockett was an American frontiersman; a 'rocket' is everyday British slang for a fierce telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Davy Crockett was a celebrated American frontiersman and folk hero.

clue.text: Company deficit — one's dealt with huge figures

parts.note: a deficit is a loss
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A company's losses are handled by someone who deals in big numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are gigantic statues, so huge figures, plural of colossus.

clue.text: Endlessly ill, upset, extremely irritable

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the piece is turned upside down, read backwards
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: extremely means very

explanation.surface: Someone constantly unwell and upset becomes very tetchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts ILL to IL and 'upset' turns that to LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is an old word for liverish, which means bad-tempered and irritable.

clue.text: A blockhead in a spin, unresponsive

indicators.note: in a spin means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a blockhead is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot is in a whirl and does not react.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and cool, holding back from response to others.

clue.text: Big fuss created by e.g., mink, valuable material

parts.note: mink is an example of a fur
ore is a valuable mined material

explanation.surface: An uproar is caused by mink coats and other luxury materials.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public anger or excitement, a big fuss.

clue.text: Woman in English society, this person

parts.note: this person is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A woman in English high society talks about herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Esme is a woman's first name, so a woman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Dog, one of the 8

definitions.meaning: a classic name given to a pet dog
a sea robber, one of the answer at 8 across

explanation.definitionFit: Rover is a traditional dog's name and also an old word for a sea raider.

clue.text: Not entirely prepared to study

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: prepared means ready

explanation.surface: Someone is not fully ready to revise.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is to study it, as at university.

clue.text: Poetic village festival enthralling a hundred all right

indicators.note: enthralling means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A village festival captivates a hundred people and goes well.
explanation.walkthrough: East Coker is a Somerset village and the title of a poem in T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets.
explanation.definitionFit: East Coker is the village that gives its name to one of Eliot's Four Quartets.

clue.text: Blessed state offered by vehicle in terrible rain

indicators.note: in means the vehicle sits inside the scrambled letters
terrible means the letters are put in a dreadful mess

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Bliss is found in a vehicle during awful rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes NIRA from the rain, and the vehicle sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect bliss, a blessed condition.

clue.text: Eastern reader who has the vote?

parts.note: a lector is a reader, especially in church or a university

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an Eastern reader is entitled to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is a person entitled to vote in an election.
